html.modes.title: Selection mode: keys 1, 2, 3, 4 or Tab / Shift+Tab
html.undo-button.title: Undo
html.redo-button.title: Redo

html.polygon-toggle.title: Polygon: draw a flat polygon point by point on the grid (G)
html.pencil-toggle.title: Pencil: draw vertices and edges, pulling them out of vertices (P)
html.place-toggle.title: Place: put an object onto another's surface, the chosen side against it

XZ plane through the object's pivot point
XY plane through the object's pivot point
html.grid-controls.grid-fine.button.titl: Fine grid: how many parts a cell is divided into while Ctrl is held
html.collision-button.title: Collisions: the objects' collision shapes for Godot — add them by hand or fit them automatically, then adjust
html.animation-button.title: Animation: objects and nodes moving by keyframes — for export to Godot
html.render-button.title: Sprite render: the model from every side into a PNG sheet for a 2D game
html.toolbar.tool-select.title: Select (Q)
html.toolbar.tool-move.title: Move (W)
html.toolbar.tool-rotate.title: Rotate (R)
html.toolbar.tool-scale.title: Scale (S)
html.toolbar.tool-pivot.title: Pivot point (D)
html.toolbar.tool-paint.title: Brush: paint on the model or on the unwrap, pixel by pixel. Shift+click — a straight line from the last point (with Space — along the model's faces), Alt+click picks a colour (V)
html.paint-color.title: Colour and palette
html.toolbar.tool-pipette.title: Pipette: pick a colour from the model or the unwrap. With any painting tool Alt+click does the same (I)
html.toolbar.tool-fill.title: Fill: paint over an area of one colour. On the model — within the face's chart, on the unwrap — over the whole picture (E)
html.shape-tool.title: Shapes: drawn out from press to release. A press opens the choice of shape
html.toolbar.tool-marquee.title: Pixel selection — on the unwrap only: drag — select a rectangle; drag from inside — move it (with Alt — a copy); Delete — erase, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V — copy, cut, paste; the unwrap's turn and flip buttons turn the selection. Enter — put down, Esc — put back
html.toolbar.action-make-face.title: Make a face through the selected vertices or edges; from two vertices — an edge (Ctrl+D)
html.toolbar.action-flip-faces.title: Flip faces: swap the front and back of the selected faces, or of all faces of the picked objects (Ctrl+I)
html.toolbar.action-delete.title: Delete the selected vertices (Delete)
html.toolbar.action-frame.title: Frame the selection (F)
html.toolbar.action-views-window.title: Views in a separate window: perspective and three views, two by two
html.toolbar.action-toggle-views.title: Three views (B)
html.toolbar.action-toggle-uv.title: UV editor: the atlas with the faces, faces rearranged on the picture
html.mode-indicator.title: Selection mode: object — cube, face — plane, edge — line, vertex — point
html.sim-restart.title: Start again
html.operation-close.title: Leave the mode (Esc)
html.place-options.place-y.title: The object's bottom (along its Y axis)
html.place-options.place-x.title: The object's −X side
html.place-options.place-z.title: The object's −Z side
html.cut-options.button.title: Vertical cut (Tab — switch)
html.axis-gizmo.title: Vertex move lock: Shift+1 — free, Shift+2 — X, Shift+3 — Y, Shift+4 — Z
html.light-button.title: Light: the model lit as in a game — a sun with shadows on the model and the floor, and the sky's ambient light. Turning the camera shows the lit and the shaded sides
html.preview-button.title: Preview: only the textured model on a black background, without the grid, edges, vertices or selection — as it will look after export
html.focus-button.title: Focus: dark background, the object a white wireframe with vertex dots, picking through the object (T)
html.shading-button.title: Object shading
html.shading-menu.shading-orientation.ti: A face's front is blue, its back red (N)
html.shading-menu.shading-textured.title: The model with the texture of the project's atlas
html.shading-menu.shading-weights.title: Skin weights: select a node (or the binding row under it) — the surface is coloured by how much it bends it: blue — not at all, red — wholly
html.polygon-popup.title: The polygon's plane: click the axis it is perpendicular to
html.extrude-popup.title: Where to extrude the edge: click an axis, the middle — automatic
html.views-splitter.title: Drag to change the panel's height; double-click — back to the default
html.ortho-views.title: LMB — drag a vertex · Shift+drag — selection box · RMB — pan · Wheel — zoom
html.anim-splitter.title: Drag to share the space between the three views and the timeline; double-click — evenly
html.timeline.uv-bar.clip-select.title: The clip you are working on
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-add.title: New clip: its name and length are asked
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-edit.title: The clip's name and length
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-duplicate.title: Duplicate the clip
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-delete.title: Delete the clip (can be undone)
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-first.title: To the start
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-prev.title: Frame back
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-play.title: Play (Enter)
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-next.title: Frame forward
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-last.title: To the end
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-loop.title: Loop: the clip plays round and round. In Godot it will loop
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-field.title: Frames per second
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-key.title: Insert a key: what was changed by hand on the selection, at this frame (K)
html.timeline.uv-bar.tl-autokey.title: Auto key: any move of an object at once sets a key at the current frame. Off — the move is temporary, K sets the key
html.timeline.tl-empty.text: No clips yet — create the first one with the «+» button above
html.timeline.tl-body.tl-corner.tl-nodes: Nodes only: the timeline shows only nodes, keys are set only on them, and a click on an object in the view selects its node. The objects' own keys stay in the clip and play, but are not shown
html.timeline.tl-body.tl-corner.tl-keyal: Key everything: position, rotation and scale of all objects and nodes at the current frame, as they are shown
html.timeline.tl-body.tl-ruler.title: Click or drag — go to a frame · wheel — scroll · Ctrl+wheel — zoom · middle button — pan
html.timeline.tl-body.tl-seconds.title: Time in seconds (frame / the clip's FPS)
html.timeline.tl-body.tl-resize.title: Drag to change the width of the names column; double-click — back to the default
html.uv-atlas-new.title: New atlas: empty, with a pixel size of its own
html.uv-atlas.title: The atlas shown here and painted on by the brush
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-add.title: Put the picked objects on the atlas: their faces get a place on the picture
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-remove.title: Take the picked objects off the atlas: their faces lose their place on the picture; what was painted for them stays until «Clean» is pressed (can be undone)
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-turn-left.title: Turn the picked charts 90° counterclockwise
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-flip-h.title: Flip the picked charts left to right
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-flip-v.title: Flip the picked charts top to bottom
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-map-turn-left.t: Turn the unwrap 90° counterclockwise: the picture on the atlas stays where it is, the face shows it turned. Square charts only
Turn the unwrap 90° clockwise: the picture on the atlas stays where it is, the face shows it turned. Square charts only
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-map-flip-h.titl: Mirror the unwrap left to right: the picture on the atlas stays where it is, the face shows it mirrored
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-map-flip-v.titl: Mirror the unwrap top to bottom: the picture on the atlas stays where it is, the face shows it mirrored
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-shape.title: Shape lock. Closed: a chart can only be moved, turned and flipped. Open: the picked charts get markers at their corners, which can be moved pixel by pixel — the face stretches with them
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-regenerate.titl: Regenerate the picked charts: pinning and changed shapes are dropped, the charts are laid out anew and filled with the template; what was painted at the old place stays until «Clean» is pressed. With nothing picked — the whole atlas. Can be undone
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-clean.title: Clean: erase from the atlas everything painted that no face shows — left over from deleted, moved and shrunk faces, and painted outside the charts. Asked first; can be undone
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-pack.title: Repack: lay all the atlas' charts out tightly, with what is painted on them, by the same rules as the unwrap; charts sharing a picture (lying on one another) move together, the picture is not duplicated; the atlas shrinks if they fit in a smaller one. Charts are not turned; what is painted outside the charts is not kept. Can be undone
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-fit.title: Show the whole atlas
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-paste.title: Paste a picture from the clipboard: it lies over the atlas at the top left (the atlas grows if needed). It can be dragged, and its corners pulled to resize it (Shift — keeping its proportions). Enter or a click outside — put it down, Esc — cancel
html.uv-editor.uv-bar.uv-retro.title: Distort: fit the texture to a palette, add dithering, noise, correct colours — «retrofication». Works on the selected pixels, or with no selection on the whole atlas; the result is shown at once, «Apply» writes it as one undo step
html.uv-editor.canvas.title: LMB — pick a chart (Shift — add) · drag — move it elsewhere on the picture · wheel — zoom · RMB — pan the view
html.panel-splitter.title: Drag to change the panel's width; double-click — back to the default
html.add-object.title: Add an object
html.outliner.title: Click — pick an object · Shift+click — add or remove · double-click — rename · drag onto an object — put it inside, onto an empty place — take it to the top
html.copy-size.title: Copy the X, Y, Z sizes as one line
html.paste-size.title: Paste the X, Y, Z sizes from the clipboard
html.center-pivot.title: Put the pivot point at the object's centre
html.copy-vector.title: Copy X, Y, Z as one line
html.paste-vector.title: Paste X, Y, Z from the clipboard
html.copy-rotation.title: Copy the X, Y, Z angles as one line
html.paste-rotation.title: Paste the X, Y, Z angles from the clipboard
html.collision-panel.collision-hint.text: Pick an object: click it or its shape
html.collision-panel.collision-body.body: What the object becomes in Godot
StaticBody3D: does not move — walls, floors, rocks
AnimatableBody3D: moved by code or animation — doors, lifts
RigidBody3D: moved by physics — crates, barrels
Area3D: stops nothing, only notices what enters — zones, pickups
html.collision-panel.collision-body.coll: Add a shape fitted to the object
A box by the object's bounds
A capsule along the object's longest axis
A cylinder along the object's longest axis
Convex hull: close-fitting, but without hollows
The object's own faces: exact, but for static bodies only — such a body cannot move in Godot
Fit the shape again to the object as it is now
The whole length, rounded ends included
html.pose-panel.properties-header.pose-k: A key of what was changed by hand, at this frame (K)
html.pose-panel.pose-group.label.pose-ro: The quaternion's W (with X, Y, Z: the direction and angle of the turn; the length is brought to one)
Angle in degrees; may be more than 360 — the object then makes several turns
Angle in degrees; may be more than 360 — the object then makes several turns
Angle in degrees; may be more than 360 — the object then makes several turns
html.object-atlas-line.title: The atlas whose picture the object is painted with. Moved to another atlas, its faces are laid out on it anew; what was painted on the old one stays there until it is cleaned
html.object-props.flag.title: Unticked — faces are seen from the front only, as most game engines draw them: from inside a closed object you see what is behind it. Goes into the export too
html.object-props.flag.title2: Unticked — faces are lit flat, every edge shows. Ticked — the light flows smoothly over edges where faces meet at less than the given angle, sharper edges stay hard. Goes into the export too
html.smooth-angle.title: Edges sharper than this angle (in degrees) are not smoothed
html.skin-node.title: The bone node to bind the selected vertices to
html.skin-bind.title: The selected vertices bend wholly with this node (weight 1). The node's pivot point is the joint
html.skin-panel.skin-weight.label.title: How much the selected vertices bend with this node: 1 — wholly, 0.5 — by half. The rest — with what they bent with (or their object's node)
html.skin-weight-set.title: Give the selected vertices this weight of the chosen node
html.skin-auto.title: Automatic weights: every selected vertex is bound to the nearest bones (a bone runs from a node's pivot point to the nodes inside it), the nearer the stronger, and the weights are smoothed. Distance is measured in a straight line: neighbouring parts (legs, say) may take from each other — correct it by binding
html.skin-smooth.title: The selected vertices' weights become like their neighbours' along the edges — the joint bends smoothly, not at one edge. Can be pressed several times
html.skin-unbind.title: The selected vertices no longer bend: they move wholly with their object
html.skin-pose.title: Trial pose: rotate, move and scale nodes with the gizmo — the mesh bends, the model does not change and no keys are set. Weights can be edited meanwhile. Off — this button or Esc
html.ppu-line.title: How many texture pixels there are to a unit of length. Set when the project is made, one value for the whole project
html.texture-section.texture-line.title: The atlas' size: it grows by itself when the faces run out of room
html.atlas-open.title: Open the atlas' picture in a painting program. A working copy of the picture goes into a temporary folder; what is saved there shows on the model at once, and goes into the project file when the project is saved. A guide file with the faces' outlines lies beside it
html.atlas-reveal.title: Show the atlas' working copy and the outlines file in their folder
html.atlas-repack.title: Lay all faces out on the atlas anew, tightly. What was painted is lost (can be undone)
html.stats-title.title: Figures of the picked objects; with nothing picked — of the whole scene
html.stats.dl.dt.title: The size of the model's data: vertex coordinates and the faces' make-up. The memory the editor takes is more.
html.errors-button.title: Errors in the model
html.warnings-button.title: Warnings about the model
html.welcome.welcome-box.welcome-head.we: Open a project from a file
html.welcome.welcome-box.welcome-empty.t: Projects you have worked on will appear here.
html.new-project-dialog.dialog.choice-ca: The whole model is painted with one picture, pixels are the same size everywhere
How many texture pixels there are to a unit of length. Can be changed later, but the unwrap is then made anew
Each object is painted with its atlas' picture, every atlas has a pixel size of its own. Atlases are made in the project, their pixel size given when they are made
html.clip-popup.label.title: The clip's name — in Latin letters: so it will be called in Godot. Empty — a name is given
html.clip-popup.label.title2: The clip's length in frames (at its FPS)
html.atlas-popup.label.title: The atlas' name, in Latin letters. Empty — a name is given
html.atlas-popup.label.title2: How many texture pixels there are to a unit of length on this atlas. Every atlas has a pixel size of its own
html.retro-popup.retro-row.title: The noise's grain size, in atlas pixels
Unticked — every channel has noise of its own, coloured
html.retro-popup.retro-row.title2: Without a palette: bring each channel down to so many levels (posterization). 0 — off
html.retro-popup.retro-check.title: Bring the colours down to a palette: every pixel takes its nearest colour (nearest to the eye). Levels do not apply then
html.retro-popup.retro-palette.name-pres: A ready palette: replaces the colours below
html.retro-popup.retro-palette.retro-lin: Add the current brush colour to the palette
Find a palette from the picture itself: as many colours as given
html.retro-popup.retro-row.title3: How strongly dithering blurs the step between colours
html.retro-popup.retro-buttons.retro-res: Put all settings back to the defaults
html.color-popup.color-field.title: Shade: to the left — paler, down — darker
html.color-popup.color-hue.title: Hue
html.color-popup.color-palette-bar.type-: Add the brush colour to the palette
Load a palette from a file: Aseprite (.aseprite, .ase), GIMP (.gpl), .pal, .hex, .act or a .png picture. Replaces the current one
html.export-dialog.dialog.field.title: How many times larger the model is in the file than in the editor: 2 — twice as large, 0.5 — half as large. The file's unit of length is a metre. The project does not change
html.export-dialog.dialog.choice.title: Needed if where the model goes, the texture is smoothed or shrunk with distance. The picture in the project itself does not change
html.export-dialog.dialog.choice.span.sm: The edge pixels of every chart are extended outwards into the atlas' empty places, so that no foreign colours show at the model's seams
html.settings-close.title: Close (Esc)
html.settings-dialog.dialog.settings-bod: How much the distance to the object changes with one click of the wheel
How long the camera takes to arrive after the wheel is turned; 0 — at once
The program the atlas' picture is opened in by the «Paint in an external editor» button: the path to its executable. Empty — the one the system opens such files with
html.external-editor-clear.title: Open with the default program
html.settings-dialog.dialog.settings-bod: The «Paint in an external editor» button in the «Texture» panel opens the atlas' picture in this program. What is saved there shows on the model at once.
html.hotkeys-reset.title: Put all keys back to the defaults
html.render-mode.render-body.render-prev: Click a frame — show it above · wheel — zoom, right or middle button — pan
Nothing to render: the scene has no visible faces
html.render-mode.render-body.render-spli: Drag to change the panel's width; double-click — back to the default
html.render-mode.render-body.render-sett: The model at rest, as in the editor: one sheet with the directions
Animation clips: for every clip and direction a PNG of its own with a strip of frames, plus SpriteFrames for Godot (.tres) and JSON
Which clip is shown in the preview. All clips go into the export
The sprite's frames per second: the clip is taken at equal steps of time. Fewer — fewer frames in the PNG
How many sides the model is taken from: frames in the sheet
The model's turn in the first frame, in degrees; then in equal steps counterclockwise, seen from above
0 — from the side, 26.57 — pixel art's 2:1 «isometry», 90 — from above
Sprite pixels per atlas pixel: at 1 the model's pixels become the sprite's pixels
The smallest frame size the model fits in from every side
How the frames lie on the sheet: in one row, no more than N columns (as many rows as needed) or no more than N rows (as many columns as needed)
The texture's pure colours, no shading — the shading is already painted in the pixels
As in the editor: light from the viewer's side, the same in every frame
Light from the chosen side, fixed in the world: as the model turns, its lit and shaded sides show
Side view: the light's height above the horizon. The sun can be dragged
Top view: which side the light comes from; the triangle below — the side of the first frame's camera. The sun can be dragged
0 — in front (the first frame's side), 90 — right, 180 — behind, 270 — left
0 — from the side, along the horizon; 90 — straight from above
In steps of brightness, with no blending between them — as in hand-drawn pixel art. Faceted objects' faces come down to so many shades, smooth ones get bands of light
How many steps of brightness from light to shadow
The steps blended by a checkerboard of the two neighbouring steps' pixels, as in pixel art (ordered dithering, a 4×4 Bayer matrix). Only where the light goes from step to step over a rounded surface
All light between the steps is checkered — a flat face too, wholly, if its lighting is between them
The sheet's width and height are 64, 128, 256…, as many engines require: a see-through margin is added at the right and bottom, the frames stay where they are
Beside the PNG — a JSON with the place and angle of every frame (TexturePacker / Aseprite format)
Save the sheet as PNG (and a JSON with frames, if ticked). With clips — a PNG for every clip and direction, SpriteFrames for Godot (.tres) and JSON
settings.language.restart: The language changes when verTEX is started again.
views.perspective.title: LMB — orbit · RMB — pan · wheel — zoom
app.hotkeys.fixed.esc: Cancel the action, leave the mode, clear the selection
app.hotkeys.fixed.tab: Next / previous selection mode; in the cut — vertical / horizontal
app.hotkeys.fixed.enter: Polygon: close the outline; pixel selection: put down what was moved
app.hotkeys.fixed.f1: Unwrap: dim the picture except the face under the pointer (on the unwrap or on the model)
app.hotkeys.fixed.alt-wheel: Extrude: widen / narrow the extruded face by a fine grid step
app.hotkeys.fixed.xcz: While dragging: along the X / Y / Z axis only
app.skin.toast.pose: Trial pose: the model is not changed

app.skin.weight.stuck.one: {count} vertex with weight 1: its object is not in a node, the rest has nowhere to go
app.skin.weight.stuck.other: {count} vertices with weight 1: their object is not in a node, the rest has nowhere to go

app.skin.summary.unbound-moves: Not in the skin — moves with its object ({parts})
app.grid.fine: A cell is divided by {divisor} — step {step}
app.settings.hotkeys.keys-title: Click, then press the new key combination · Esc — leave as it is
app.settings.hotkeys.fixed-key: {keys} is a fixed key, it can't be assigned
app.settings.hotkeys.taken: {keys} belonged to «{action}» — it is left without a key
app.mirror.not-one: more than one object is being edited
app.mirror.title.off: Mirror: off. Edits are repeated on the other side of a plane
app.export.gltf.title: Export to glTF
app.export.restart: Export will work after the program is restarted.
app.export.nothing.detail: The scene has no visible faces.
app.atlas.row.title: Atlas «{name}»: {ppu} px per unit, {width} × {height}. Click — work with it, double-click the name — rename
app.atlas.remove.title: Delete the atlas: its objects are left without a texture (can be undone)
app.atlas.add.title: New atlas: empty, with a pixel size of its own. Objects are moved onto it — in their properties or with a button in the UV editor

app.atlas.remove.detail.one: {count} object will be left without a texture, what is painted on the atlas will be lost. Can be undone.
app.atlas.remove.detail.other: {count} objects will be left without a texture, what is painted on the atlas will be lost. Can be undone.

app.atlas.remove.detail-empty: What is painted on it will be lost. Can be undone.
app.atlas.repack.message: Lay out all the faces on the atlas anew?
app.atlas.repack.detail: Everything painted on the texture will be lost. Can be undone.
app.retro.swatch.title: {color} — click to remove from the palette
app.local-axes.on: Local axes on: moving and rotating go along the object's own axes ({keys}). Click to go back to the world's
app.local-axes.off: Local axes off: moving and rotating go along the world's axes ({keys}). Click to turn them on
app.snapping.on: Grid snapping on: moving and scaling go by grid steps. Click to turn it off
app.snapping.off: Grid snapping off: moving and scaling are free. Click to turn it on
outliner.join.title: Join objects from different atlases?
outliner.join.text: The joined object will be on the atlas «{atlas}»; faces from the other atlases are laid out on it anew, what was painted for them stays on the old ones. Can be undone.
outliner.side.auto.label: Auto
outliner.side.auto.title: The side of the selected faces, or the one facing the camera
outliner.row.node.title: Node: {count} inside
outliner.lock.shut.title: Node shut: in the main view a click on any of its parts selects the whole node (in the tree and the three views the parts are selected as usual). Click — «nearest node»
outliner.lock.nearest.title: Nearest node: in the main view a click on an object in it selects the nearest node above it in the hierarchy. Click to open
outliner.lock.open.title: Node open: its parts are selected one by one. Click to shut it — then in the main view it is selected whole
outliner.add-into.title: Create an object in this node
outliner.shape.title: Collision shape: click — select, double-click — rename, Delete — delete
outliner.skin.title: Vertices of «{object}» bound to «{node}»: click — select them and set their weight in the «Skin» panel
outliner.attach.title: The new object will be put right up against the selected one, on the side chosen
outliner.attach.none.title: Nothing is selected: the object will appear at the origin
outliner.attach.caption: Up against the selection
outliner.side.title: On the {side} side of the selected object
outliner.field.range.title: from {min} to {max} · to change it, drag the dot on the right up or down
timeline.track.select.position: Select it and take the move tool (W)
timeline.track.select.rotation: Select it and take the rotate tool (R)
timeline.track.select.scale: Select it and take the scale tool (S)
timeline.loop.off.title: No loop: the clip plays once. Click — loop
timeline.loop.on.title: Loop: the clip plays round and round, in Godot it will loop. Click — ping-pong
timeline.loop.pingpong.title: Ping-pong: the clip plays forward, then back, round and round. In Godot it is a loop twice as long, the way back written into it. Click — no loop
timeline.restore.lost.title: Bring back the pose changed at frame {frame} and dropped without a key
timeline.restore.pending.title: Not keyed: the pose is changed but no key is set — when the frame changes it drops back to where the ghost is shown (K — set a key). After that it can be brought back here
timeline.restore.title: Bring back the pose: if a pose changed without a key drops back when the frame changes, it can be brought back here
timeline.rotation.quaternion.title: Rotation by quaternions (W, X, Y, Z): the shortest way, no «gimbal lock», but no more than half a turn between keys. Click — switch to angles
timeline.rotation.euler.title: Rotation by angles (X, Y, Z): more than 360° between keys is possible, but turning about several axes the path may be crooked. Click — switch to quaternions
timeline.key-popup.grip.title: Drag to move the window
timeline.key-popup.prev.title: The track's previous key
timeline.key-popup.next.title: The track's next key
timeline.key-popup.close.title: Close (Esc)
timeline.curve.title: Transition curve
timeline.curve.graph.title: The curve of the transition to the next key: drag the handles to make your own
timeline.curve.default.title: Gentle speeding up and slowing down (smoothstep)
timeline.curve.custom.title: A custom curve: set by the handles on the graph
timeline.curve.in.title: Ease in: slow at the start
timeline.curve.out.title: Ease out: slow at the end
timeline.curve.inout.title: Ease in and out
timeline.preview.title: Preview: the transition from this key to the next, round and round, with a second of pause at the start and the end
timeline.preview.none.title: Preview: this track has no key after this one
